title: Lat Pulldown
summary: A seated cable pull from overhead: the pull-up pattern at any load. Lats 1, with biceps and mid-back helping.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: lat pulldown station (seat and thigh pad).

muscles.why: The lats pull the upper arm down toward the body; at the top, arms straight, they are fully stretched.
The elbow flexors bend the elbow; overhand grip, so they help (0.5).
Mid-back pulls the shoulder blades down and back at the bottom.
Rear delts help extend the shoulder: minor.

setup.text: Set the thigh pad so your legs are locked in.
Grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Sit tall, chest up, with a slight lean back.

form_cues.why: A small lean lines the pull up with the lats; a big one turns it into a row.

form_cues.cue: Pull the bar to your upper chest
form_cues.why: Upper chest is the end of the range for most lifters.

form_cues.cue: Let the arms fully extend at the top
form_cues.why: Full extension at the top is the stretch.

form_cues.cue: Don't yank with your lower back. Pull from your elbows.
form_cues.why: Pulling with the elbows keeps the lats, not the lower back, moving the weight.

form_cues.cue: Drive the elbows down to your sides
form_cues.why: That is the lat's line of pull.

bias_tweaks.effect: Coaches use it for 'width'; the lat is one muscle, so this is a tendency.
bias_tweaks.caveat: EMG was similar across grip widths, and wide grips allow less load.

bias_tweaks.effect: More elbow flexion and often a stronger pull.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Grip choice changes little for the lats.

bias_tweaks.effect: More range and a longer stretch per side.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Leaning way back and rowing the bar to your stomach.
mistakes.fix: Stay nearly upright and pull to the upper chest.

mistakes.text: Letting the stack pull your arms up fast.
mistakes.fix: Control the top; that is the stretch.

mistakes.text: Pulling the bar behind the neck.
mistakes.fix: Pull to the front; it lets the lats work without forcing the shoulders.

misconceptions.myth: Behind-the-neck pulldowns hit the lats harder.
misconceptions.reality: No growth advantage has been shown; pulling to the front is the standard.

misconceptions.myth: Machines don't build muscle like free weights.
misconceptions.reality: Free-weight and machine training gave similar muscle growth in a meta-analysis. Pick by fit, stability and how well you can push close to failure.

lower_risk.text: The app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the first working load is at least 40 kg (95 lb) and the main muscle is not already warm from an earlier lift. Otherwise start with a slightly lighter first set.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 8-12 rep range. Easy to push close to failure; stop when you start leaning back to finish reps.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: The same pattern with bodyweight; no machine needed.
One arm at a time for a longer stretch.
Lats without the biceps; low fatigue.
A horizontal pull with more mid-back (upper back 1).

notes: Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
